summary: Hash maps/sets turn 'have I seen this / how many times' into O(1). The workhorse pattern is prefix-sum + hashmap for subarray-sum questions (zero-sum, sum equals B) — store counts of running prefix sums, seeded with {0:1}. Sets give O(1) membership for run-based problems like longest consecutive sequence.

thoughtProcess.title: Subarray-sum question? Prefix sum + hashmap of counts.
thoughtProcess.body: If prefix[j] - prefix[i] == target, a subarray sums to target. Store how many times each prefix sum occurred; for each j add count[prefix[j]-target]. Seed the map with {0:1} for subarrays starting at index 0.

thoughtProcess.title: 'Longest run / consecutive' -> dump into a set, expand only from run starts.
thoughtProcess.body: Put all numbers in a HashSet. A number x starts a run only if x-1 is absent; then count x, x+1, x+2... Each number is visited O(1) times overall -> O(N).

thoughtProcess.title: Choose the container by the question: Set for membership, Map for a value.
thoughtProcess.body: HashSet = distinct/seen. HashMap = need a count, index, or first-position. Use getOrDefault/merge for frequency maps.

keyPatterns.name: Prefix sum + hashmap
keyPatterns.when: Count / longest subarray with a given sum (incl. zero)
keyPatterns.template: map={0:-1 or 0:1}; run=0; for i: run+=A[i]; check map for run-target; update map

keyPatterns.name: Set-based run expansion
keyPatterns.template: set=all; for x in set: if !set.contains(x-1): grow y=x while set.contains(y+1); track length

keyPatterns.name: Frequency map / order map
keyPatterns.when: Count occurrences, sort by given order
keyPatterns.template: freq via map.merge(x,1,Integer::sum); emit per a reference order

commonMistakes.title: Comparing boxed Integer counts with ==
commonMistakes.why: Integer autoboxing caches only -128..127, so == works by luck for small values and breaks above 127; use equals or compare primitive int.

commonMistakes.title: Prefix-sum map not seeded / wrong index convention
commonMistakes.why: Without the empty-prefix seed you miss every subarray that starts at index 0.

edgeCases: Longest-subarray-by-length: store the FIRST index of each prefix sum (don't overwrite) so the span is maximal.
Count-of-subarrays: store counts and accumulate — a prefix sum can recur many times.
Negative numbers are fine for prefix-sum+map (unlike two-pointer windows).
Longest consecutive: duplicates in the input must not inflate the run length (a set dedupes them).
